hook: Being self-aware doesn't protect you from negative thoughts. For a lot of introspective people, it makes the problem worse.
topic: The introspection trap — why self-awareness without technique amplifies spirals
body:
**There is a version of self-awareness that functions as a trap.**

You've read the books. You understand your patterns. You can narrate your thought spirals in real time — "there I go again, catastrophising." And yet the knowing doesn't stop it. If anything, you now have a thought spiral with a running commentary. Two processes, not one.

This is what happens when self-awareness becomes an additional layer of monitoring rather than a tool for change. The attention you bring to the spiral feeds it. Introspective people are often the worst affected by rumination precisely because they're very good at sustained internal attention — and that skill, applied without the right technique, becomes fuel.

The missing piece isn't more insight. You probably have enough of that. The missing piece is the moment of disengagement. The practice of noticing a thought — and then choosing where to put your attention next, rather than examining the thought further.

Self-awareness is the noticing. What comes after the noticing is the work.

You can't think your way out of overthinking.

Five-step guide for what comes after the noticing — link in bio.
